title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure carried by synthetic video. A fabricated broadcast was made to look like reporting from Mother Jones, using the outlet's logo and fake footage of its editor, and it asserted as fact that the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to a CNN executive. The impersonation did not sit inside any newsroom's process. It entered at the distribution layer, on X, through accounts that posted it to an audience before any check on the claim or the footage.

Catching it before that reach required either the platform to act on the impersonation itself or the outlet to notice and complain. Mother Jones did complain, and X removed the reported post under its trademark policy, which addresses the misuse of a mark rather than the truth of the claim. Researchers separately pointed to bot-like account behaviour and inflated view counts as signs the reach was not organic, so signals of inauthentic amplification were available alongside the impersonation.

What is not established is intent or effect. The assessment that the campaign appears meant to help Donald Trump and Republicans is an assessment, the reading of the view counts as inflated is a researcher judgement, and the removal was a trademark action, not a finding on whether the video's claim was true.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network called Matryoshka, also known as Storm-1679, spread a fake Mother Jones video before the 2026 midterms. The video falsely claimed the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN head Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. It used a Mother Jones logo and fake footage of editor Clara Jeffery. An X account named роман posted it, and it got 155,000 views, while another account got 50,000. Researchers said the accounts and view counts showed signs of bots and inflated reach. Mother Jones complained to X, which removed the reported post for violating its trademark policy.

The network has posted deepfakes of celebrities and fake news reports about Democratic candidates, often pretending to come from US outlets. The campaign appears meant to help Donald Trump and Republicans. So far, this operation has not gained major reach on X, Bluesky, or other platforms. The article warns that Russian influence efforts may continue, especially because the Trump administration closed government units that tracked foreign disinformation. It says this could affect the midterms and create more chaos.
